name: Tirumular
credit: No authentic portrait is known · Tamil text from Tamil Wikisource (CC BY-SA transcription; the underlying text is public domain)
bio: Tirumular is the name given to the Siddhar, a Shaiva yogi and sage, who composed the Tirumantiram, the tenth book of the Tirumurai, the twelve-book canon of Tamil Shaiva devotional writing. Tradition says he was a yogi from the Himalayan north who entered the body of a dead cowherd named Mulan, to be able to teach, and so became known as Tirumular, the holy Mulan. His dates are uncertain; he is traditionally placed in the fifth or sixth century, though many scholars date the work later.

The Tirumantiram runs to about three thousand quatrains, divided after an invocation and a preface into nine tantras. It sets out Shaiva doctrine, yoga, the worship of Shiva and the path to liberation in a single teaching, and is counted among the founding texts of Tamil Shaiva Siddhanta. Here appear the invocation, the preface and the nine tantras in the original Tamil.
